title: Aluvihare Rock Temple
geometryBasis: Named OSM way 1197751507 outlines the narrow northwest-southeast temple cleft, between four specifically mapped bare-rock outcrops. Shared vertices and the Southeast entry from the road fix the approach and constrain the left veranda and inner stair.
sectionBasis: Cave’s eyewitness account places the tiled veranda on the left of the approach, with a cavern behind it. His photograph fixes the basic masonry, stair sequence and overhanging rock; component sizes, hidden backs and the alignment within the modern map are estimated.
limitations: The model depicts the photographed temple cleft in 1896. Rock plans follow present mapped outcrops. Heights, fractures, beyond-entrance volumes, and the reconstruction of the small upper shrine are estimated.
The heightfield is preserved independently. Its broad slope is used for terrain registration. Local passage and stair grades are approximate, with a bounded cut confined to the approach and cleft.

The modeled scope is the visible sanctuary entrance, stone steps, and adjacent rock faces. Buried cave rooms, murals, present-day annexes, and other parts of the monastery are outside the representation.
